sections.content:
You know hedging from B2 Unit 21 and stance adverbs such as *precisamente* and *francamente* from B2 Unit 1. When you read between the lines of an email, speech or review, these expressions separate what a message says on the surface from what it signals underneath.

• *en apariencia* and *aparentemente* mark the surface reading while signalling that the speaker is cautious or expects a contrast: *En apariencia, el mensaje es cordial; en el fondo, expresa un reproche.*
• *en el fondo* ('deep down / underneath') introduces the underlying attitude or real meaning behind a polite or subtle phrasing.
• Stance adverbs like *francamente*, *precisamente* and *aparentemente* stand outside the core verb phrase (usually set off by commas when sentence-initial) to comment on the whole statement: *Francamente, esa connotación no pasa desapercibida.*

sections.title: Surface vs. underlying stance markers
rows: En apariencia, aceptó la propuesta sin problemas.
Aparentemente, la frase no tiene ninguna connotación negativa.
En el fondo, su tono sutil revela cierto desacuerdo.
Francamente, conviene leer entre líneas antes de responder.

items.spanish: En apariencia, la nota es neutral; en el fondo, tiene una connotación crítica muy sutil.
items.english: On the surface, the note is neutral; underneath, it has a very subtle critical connotation.

items.spanish: Aparentemente, todos estuvieron de acuerdo, pero faltó franqueza en la reunión.
items.english: Apparently, everyone agreed, but there was a lack of candour in the meeting.

items.spanish: Francamente, hay que leer entre líneas para captar la intención real de ese correo.
items.english: Frankly, you have to read between the lines to grasp the real intention of that email.

items.spanish: Precisamente esa palabra sutil explica por qué cambió el tono del mensaje.
items.english: Precisely that subtle word explains why the tone of the message changed.

sections.content: Place a comma after sentence-initial stance markers (*Aparentemente, ...*, *En apariencia, ...*, *En el fondo, ...*, *Francamente, ...*). Notice also that *en apariencia* sets up a contrast with what lies beneath (*en el fondo*), so it rarely stands alone as an unqualified endorsement.
